_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2016: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2015 state of the verified 2015 register (China's ~3% objective of 5 Mar 2015; the FOMC's 2% goal, the BoJ's 2% target, the RBA's Statement of 24 Oct 2013, New Zealand's 2012 PTA), plus the 2016 current-year targets set earlier: Türkiye 5% (CBRT policy document of 24 Dec 2013, para 1: 'the inflation target for 2016 is set as 5 percent'); Brazil 4.5% ±2 (CMN Res. 4,345 of 25 Jun 2014); Colombia 3% ±1 (Board of 27 Nov 2015); Indonesia 4% ±1 (PMK 93/PMK.011/2014, promulgated 3 Jun 2014); Korea 2% (MPC of 16 Dec 2015, replacing 2.5–3.5%); Thailand 2.5% ±1.5 (Cabinet, 29 Dec 2015; BoT announcement of 30 Dec 2015); India 5% (RBI, 29 Sep 2015: 'around 5 per cent by the end of fiscal' [the year ending in March of the following calendar year], the glide-path objective of below 6 per cent by January having reached its horizon). Changes announced during 2016: China's annual objective (5 Mar 2016: around 3%, value unchanged, recorded for its wording), the Indian statutory inflation target of 4% ±2 (notified 5 Aug 2016; value unchanged at 5, the RBI's current-year objective, reaffirmed by the MPC on 4 Oct 2016) and the RBA's new Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy (19 Sep 2016; value unchanged, recorded for its wording). Value-unchanged reaffirmations (the FOMC's January statement of longer-run goals, the UK remit of 16 Mar 2016, Poland's guidelines) and targets set during 2016 for later years (Canada's renewal of 24 Oct 2016) are not recorded. Every new source was fetched and its quoted text checked (the Bank of Thailand announcement is a scanned PDF, its Thai text transcribed; Colombia's release was read through a fetch service behind the bank's bot check); sources are shown only once published; no wording names a later year.
note: One economy has no headline-CPI target: the Federal Reserve's statements refer to the PCE price index (see its row; the benchmark is applied to headline CPI). India's benchmark is the RBI's end-of-fiscal-year CPI objective. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, 25 Jan 2012: 'The Committee judges that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate.'
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy, 25 Jan 2012

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada, 8 Nov 2011: 'The inflation target will continue to be the 2 per cent mid-point of the 1 to 3 per cent inflation-control range'; the agreement was renewed for another five-year period.

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 8 Nov 2011

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 24 Oct 2013: 'both the Reserve Bank and the Government agree on the objective of keeping consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over the cycle' (midpoint 2.5%).

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 24 Oct 2013

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: 'The annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) is to be two per cent', tolerance band ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2007:3, October 2007
Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2008:1, February 2008

NO.wording: 'Annual consumer price inflation of approximately 2.5% over time.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 3/07

NZ.wording: Policy Targets Agreement signed 20 Sep 2012: 'The agreement continues to require the Reserve Bank to keep CPI inflation between 1 per cent and 3 per cent on average over the medium term. Within this target, the new agreement now requires the Bank to focus on keeping future average inflation near 2 per cent.'

urls.label: Minister of Finance press release, 'New Policy Targets Agreement signed today', 20 Sep 2012 (Scoop)

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2015: 'keep the increase in the CPI at around 3%' (the previous year's objective, which applies until the new annual objective is announced; a government objective, not a PBoC target).

urls.label: The State Council, Report on the Work of the Government, delivered 5 Mar 2015 (full text)

IN.wording: RBI Fourth Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2015–16, Governor's statement, 29 Sep 2015 (para 15): 'the focus should now shift to bringing inflation to around 5 per cent by the end of fiscal' [the year ending in March of the following calendar year]. The glide-path objective of below 6 per cent CPI inflation by January of the current year (28 Jan 2014) has reached its horizon, so this end-of-fiscal-year objective is the benchmark for the current year; the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement's 4 per cent ±2 applies over the medium term.

urls.label: RBI press release, Fourth Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2015–16, by Dr. Raghuram G. Rajan, Governor, 29 Sep 2015 (para 15)
RBI press release 2014–2015/1847, Statement by Dr. Raghuram G Rajan, Governor, on Monetary Policy, 4 Mar 2015 (the monetary policy framework agreement)

BR.wording: CMN: 'É fixada, para o ano de 2016, a meta para a inflação de 4,5% (quatro inteiros e cinco décimos por cento), com intervalo de tolerância de menos dois pontos percentuais e de mais dois pontos percentuais'.

urls.label: CMN Resolution 4,345 of 25 Jun 2014 (2016 target)

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: IMF Public Information Notice 07/140, Mexico Article IV, 13 Dec 2007
Banxico Inflation Report October–December 2007 and Monetary Program for 2008

ZA.wording: Budget Speech, 17 Feb 2010: 'I wish to confirm that the Reserve Bank will continue to pursue a target for CPI inflation of 3 to 6 per cent' (midpoint 4.5%).

urls.label: Minister of Finance, Budget Speech 2010, 17 Feb 2010

TR.wording: End-2016 CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's policy document of 24 Dec 2013 (para 1): 'as was the case for the 2014-2015 period, the inflation target for 2016 is set as 5 percent as per the agreement reached with the government during the preparation of the Medium Term Program (MTP)'; uncertainty band ±2 percentage points (para 2).

urls.label: CBRT, Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2014, 24 Dec 2013 (paras 1–2)

PL.wording: Continuous CPI target of 2.5% with a symmetric ±1 percentage-point band, restated in the Monetary Policy Council's monetary policy guidelines (resolution of 30 Sep 2009, published 14 Oct 2009).

urls.label: Monitor Polski No. 66, item 868: MPC resolution of 30 Sep 2009 on monetary policy guidelines (published 14 Oct 2009)

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

urls.label: MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, November 2007
MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, February 2008

CZ.wording: 'The CNB announces the new inflation target as annual consumer price index growth of 2% (with a tolerance band of ± 1%), effective from January 2010'.

urls.label: CNB press release, 'The CNB's new inflation target and changes in monetary policy communication', 8 Mar 2007
CNB press release, 'The CNB issues Inflation Report I/2010', 12 Feb 2010 (the new inflation target of 2%)

ID.wording: Inflation target for 2016 of 4% with a deviation of 1%, fixed by Finance Minister Regulation 93/PMK.011/2014 (set 21 May 2014, promulgated 3 Jun 2014): '4,0% (empat persen) untuk tahun 2016' … 'dengan deviasi sebesar 1,0% (satu persen)' (annual CPI inflation, year-on-year).

urls.label: Peraturan Menteri Keuangan 93/PMK.011/2014 on the CPI inflation targets, promulgated 3 Jun 2014

KR.wording: Medium-term inflation target set by the Monetary Policy Committee on 16 Dec 2015 for the three years from 2016: 2% in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index ('소비자물가 상승률(전년 동기 대비) 기준 2%'), replacing the 2.5–3.5% range of the previous three years.

urls.label: Pressian (Yonhap), Bank of Korea lowers its medium-term inflation target to 2% (in Korean), 16 Dec 2015
Bank of Korea, financial-market note (in Korean), 17 Dec 2015: markets noting the Bank's new medium-term inflation target of 2%

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'

urls.label: Central Bank of Chile, Monetary Policy in an Inflation Targeting Framework, January 2007

CO.wording: Target for 2016 reiterated by the Board on 27 Nov 2015: 'Junta Directiva del Banco de la República reitera meta de inflación de 3% (+/- 1 punto porcentual) para 2016' … 'el Banco de la República reitera que su meta de inflación es 3%'.

urls.label: Banco de la República, Board of Directors press release (meta de inflación para 2016), 27 Nov 2015

TH.wording: Monetary-policy target for 2016 approved by the Cabinet on 29 Dec 2015, as agreed between the Monetary Policy Committee and the Minister of Finance: annual average headline inflation of 2.5 ± 1.5 percent as the inflation target for 2016 and as the medium-term monetary-policy target ('อัตราเงินเฟ้อทั่วไปเฉลี่ยทั้งปีที่ร้อยละ 2.5 ± 1.5 เป็นเป้าหมายเงินเฟ้อสำหรับปี 2559 และเป็นเป้าหมายนโยบายการเงินระยะปานกลางด้วย').

urls.label: Bank of Thailand, MPC announcement on the monetary-policy target for 2016 (in Thai), 30 Dec 2015: Cabinet approval of 29 Dec 2015

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2016, main development targets for this year: 'CPI increase kept at around 3%' (a government objective, not a PBoC target; the previous year's was also around 3%).

urls.label: Beijing Review, 'Highlights of Chinese Government Work Report for 2016', 5 Mar 2016
Report on the Work of the Government, delivered 5 Mar 2016 (full text, Embassy of China in the US)

IN.wording: Inflation target fixed by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI under section 45ZA of the RBI Act and notified in the Gazette on 5 Aug 2016: 'Inflation Target: Four per cent. Upper tolerance level: Six per cent. Lower tolerance level: Two per cent', for a period of about five years from the notification. For the current year the RBI's objective of around 5 per cent CPI inflation by the end of the fiscal year (29 Sep 2015) remains the benchmark.

urls.label: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Finance, 'Central Government in consultation with RBI announces the Inflation Target of Four Percent', 5 Aug 2016
RBI press release, Fourth Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2015–16, by Dr. Raghuram G. Rajan, Governor, 29 Sep 2015 (para 15)

RBI, Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 4 Oct 2016: 'the objective of achieving consumer price index (CPI) inflation at 5 per cent by Q4' of the fiscal year 'and the medium-term target of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent'

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016: 'They agree that an appropriate goal is to keep consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over time' (midpoint 2.5%; the previous Statement said 'over the cycle').

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016
